summary: Internal SE enablement focused on sharpening messaging, practicing a short demo that contrasts hosted vs dedicated routing, and rehearsing answers for common security/compliance questions. We hit a few rough spots in the demo script around fallback policies and KV cache explanation - Leo will record a polished clip. Group agreed on clarifying the cost/latency tradeoff and adding a one-pager for SOC2/KMS FAQs.
topics: Demo practice: routing policies, dedicated vs hosted, fallback behavior
Security/compliance talking pts: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs
transcript: [00:00:00] Samira Khan: okay everyone we're gonna start in about 30 seconds, uh thanks for joining the SE enablement session, today is messaging and demo practice
[00:00:12] Leo Martinez: hey all, quick note this is a practice run so don't be shy on interrupting and throwing questions
[00:00:20] Jenna (Observer): sounds good

[00:00:30] Samira Khan: first up messaging refresh - the two lines we want to land are performance-centric and economics-centric, like 'predictable inference economics' and 'production-grade latency', comments?
[00:00:47] Priya Patel: i like predictable inference economics, maybe we call out routing explicitly? e.g., 'smart routing for latency and cost'
[00:00:55] Leo Martinez: yeah but careful, too many buzzwords could confuse product teams - lead with problems: 'unpredictable latency and wild cost spikes'
[00:01:08] Marcus Li: also call out deployment options quickly - hosted, dedicated, private - customers ask right away if they need VPC
[00:01:20] Samira Khan: good point, maybe a single sentence that enumerates modes then pivot to benefits
[00:02:05] Samira Khan: ok demo practice - Leo will run through a 3-minute scenario showing routing between hosted and a dedicated pool, and fallback to a lower-cost variant if capacity is tight

[00:02:14] Leo Martinez: starting demo script now - 'customer request comes in, policy chooses low-latency route when SLA requires it, otherwise cost-optimized model' - um i'm stumbling on how to explain prefix caching and KV cache
[00:02:36] Priya Patel: simple language: prefix caching stores previous conversation for faster reuse, KV cache is like a memory of token embeddings that avoids recomputing the prompt every time
[00:02:48] Leo Martinez: got it, i'll say 'KV cache keeps recent tokens hot so repeated prompts are faster'
[00:03:05] Samira Khan: quick interruption - competitor note: if they ask about OpenAI or Anthropic, steer to our multi-deployment story and predictable unit economics
[00:03:20] Leo Martinez: also mention model variants - we can fallback to quantized or smaller variant to preserve uptime under load
[00:03:35] Priya Patel: someone asked about encryption at rest - mention KMS support and customer-managed keys
[00:03:47] Marcus Li: and audit logs + RBAC for enterprise, yeah
[00:04:10] Samira Khan: good. now an objection rehearsal: customer says 'Latency trumps cost for us' - what's our angle?
[00:04:20] Leo Martinez: empathize, show low-latency routing and SLOs, then show cost controls - like canary to dedicated pool to guarantee latency while keeping bulk on hosted
[00:04:36] Priya Patel: add the fallback policy example: maintain a small dedicated reserve for peak spikes so cost is bounded
[00:04:49] Samira Khan: example wording: 'we can reserve a dedicated pool for your highest priority routes and route best-effort traffic to cost-optimized variants'
[00:05:10] Observer Omar: when customers ask about Bedrock or AWS, say we integrate into their infra but our runtime focuses on kernel-level inference optimizations and smart routing
[00:05:25] Leo Martinez: ok demo round 2, i'm scripting the demo steps, i'll start the recording after we confirm language
[00:05:40] Samira Khan: let's role-play Q&A - Nina as the VP product (Priya playing), ask about compliance and residency
[00:06:00] Priya Patel (as VP Product): do you support data residency and on-prem?
[00:06:08] Leo Martinez: yes, we offer private deployment and on-prem package, plus VPC and region pinning - note: we should not promise specific region dates without checking
[00:06:22] Samira Khan: right, always caveat with 'we can discuss regions/TPG with account team'
[00:06:40] Priya Patel: another common customer question: how do you measure token costs across routing?
[00:06:48] Leo Martinez: explain per-token accounting, per-route analytics in the console and how batching/kv caching reduces effective tokens
[00:07:05] Marcus Li: small transcription note - we should avoid saying 'kv cash' in demos, it sounds wrong in calls, use 'KV cache' or 'token cache'
[00:07:18] Leo Martinez: noted, thanks

[00:08:00] Samira Khan: now competitive script - quick bullets: OpenAI = breadth and scale, ours = production-first inference + deployment flexibility; Anthropic = safety focus, ours = cost controls and observability; Bedrock = cloud integrated but limited routing/fallback flexibility

[00:08:28] Priya Patel: add an example customer story line: 'Customer X moved from multiple endpoints to single Redwood runtime and reduced per-token cost by 30% while preserving 99.9% SLO' - keep it high level
[00:08:45] Leo Martinez: practice answering 'why not just use OpenAI if they're cheaper' - point out unpredictable throughput and lack of dedicated capacity guarantees

[00:09:05] Samira Khan: good. demo walkthrough again: step 1 inbound request, step 2 policy checks, step 3 routes to dedicated if SLA, step 4 if dedicated saturated, fallback to quantized variant. highlight observability in step 5
[00:09:25] Leo Martinez: i'll add trace ids and console screenshots to show token-level breakdowns - i'll capture static screenshots so we can embed in deck
[00:09:50] Marcus Li: someone asked earlier about SOC2 attestation - what's the short answer?
[00:09:58] Priya Patel: short: Redwood is SOC2 compliant (Type II), we have audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integrations - follow up with security docs
[00:10:15] Samira Khan: action: Priya will compile an AE FAQ that has exact phrasing and doc links for security questions
[00:10:30] Leo Martinez: demo flub - i forgot to show automatic prefix caching fallback, let's rerun that segment
[00:10:45] Leo Martinez: (restarts) inbound long conversation example, prefix cache reuse reduces tokens by reusing session context, KV cache keeps keys for quick access
[00:11:05] Samira Khan: good eh, audience seemed to like the shorter phrasing, keep it under 20 seconds
[00:11:28] Observer Jenna: small nit - avoid saying 'quantization kills quality' that sounds negative, say 'quantized variants trade small quality for cost but retain core fidelity'
[00:11:42] Leo Martinez: noted, will rephrase
[00:12:10] Marcus Li: competitive question practice: 'what about model freshness and version pinning' - we support model pinning and rollouts per route
[00:12:25] Priya Patel: and automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants if pinned version is unavailable
[00:12:40] Samira Khan: ok let's do a mock customer objection: Derek (Priya) asks 'we need on-prem and HSM support, can you do that'
[00:12:50] Priya Patel (as Derek): yes but follow up with firm dates
[00:12:55] Leo Martinez: answer: yes we have an on-prem package and KMS/HSM integrations, but schedule and sizing need engineering scoping - offer a POC
[00:13:10] Samira Khan: excellent. wrap-up notes - what else to add to the deck?
[00:13:20] Priya Patel: add a short slide on cost controls: batching, caching, quantization profiles and routing policy
[00:13:30] Leo Martinez: and a one-slide competitive matrix vs OpenAI/Anthropic/Bedrock
[00:13:40] Marcus Li: also add a 'talking bullets' slide for compliance questions
[00:14:05] Samira Khan: ok final run-through for demo pacing, Leo will record two short clips: 1) routing + observability 2) fallback + KV cache - people ok with that?
[00:14:20] Group: yes
[00:14:30] Samira Khan: any other practice Qs?
[00:14:40] Leo Martinez: one more - how to handle pricing asks: say high-level ranges and offer to send detailed pricing after intake, do not give firm discounts without sales approval
[00:14:58] Priya Patel: agreed, reference the pricing playbook
[00:15:10] Samira Khan: great. recap of next steps and owners - we'll do a follow-up recording session on 2026-12-22, and Marcus will set the calendar. Thanks everyone, session ended
[00:15:25] System: meeting recording stopped
